title: Civic participation can rebound in reach while thinning in time
source_unit: Census Bureau Current Population Survey Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement, analyzed by Census Bureau and AmeriCorps

informal_neighbor_help_2023.unit: percent reporting help or exchanged favors with neighbors

observations.method: Published summary statistics from the 2023 CPS Civic Engagement and Volunteering Supplement; formal organizational volunteering and informal neighbor help are retained as separate activities.
observations.uncertainty: The activity windows and denominators differ across measures. Repeated cross-sectional estimates do not identify matched-person change, causal drivers, or whether help was adequate or sustained.
observations.subgroup: U.S. population age 16 and older; the source also reports virtual or hybrid volunteering among formal volunteers.
observations.counterinterpretation: The rebound may partly reflect recovery from pandemic lows rather than a durable increase in civic capacity; informal help may substitute for or supplement formal organizations.

observations.period: 2017 through 2023; annual time intensity among formal volunteers

denominator.unit: formal volunteers in the relevant CPS supplement estimates

observations.method: Published comparison of volunteer time intensity and online or hybrid participation; hours are not interpreted as service quality or organizational effectiveness.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison does not reveal who reduced hours, why hours changed, whether online work replaced travel, or whether shorter commitments reduced or improved local capacity.
observations.subgroup: Formal volunteers, with an online/hybrid versus in-person-only comparison; subgroup composition and task mix may differ.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower average hours can reflect broader entry into volunteering, changing task design, more flexible participation, or reduced capacity caused by work, care, health, money, or transport constraints.

related_sources.claim: The Census Bureau released the 2023 CEV microdata and describes its civic-engagement measures.
AmeriCorps headline tables provide the reported participation and time-intensity comparisons.

boundary: This record establishes a broad participation-and-time pattern, not a matched-person panel or a measure of civic efficacy, trust, belonging, policy influence, local repair, volunteer retention, or later political action. Formal volunteering and informal neighbor help are separate denominators.
